questions.question: What is the fundamental building block of nearly all modern digital integrated circuits?
options: Transistor
Resistor
Capacitor
Inductor
Diode

questions.question: In the context of a pipelined processor, what is primarily meant by a 'data hazard'?
options: When an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction that has not yet completed its execution.
When two instructions try to access the same hardware resource (e.g., an ALU) simultaneously.
When the control unit cannot determine the next instruction to fetch due to a branch instruction.
When the processor needs to fetch an instruction or data from a slower memory hierarchy level.
When there is not enough memory to store all the data required by an instruction.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'power integrity' analysis in the physical design phase of an Integrated Circuit?
options: To ensure that the power and ground distribution networks can deliver stable and sufficient voltage levels to all gates and functional blocks across the entire chip.
To minimize the total dynamic power consumption of the chip by identifying and optimizing switching activities.
To verify that all clock signals arrive at their destination flip-flops simultaneously, preventing clock skew.
To check for short circuits between power and ground rails that could lead to chip failure.
To optimize the placement and sizing of decoupling capacitors to improve signal integrity on high-speed data paths.

questions.question: In computer architecture, what does the 'locality of reference' principle primarily state regarding memory access patterns?
options: Programs tend to access data and instructions that are spatially or temporally close to those they have recently accessed.
The principle that all data must reside in the CPU's local cache before it can be processed.
A method for determining which cache block to evict based on its distance from the CPU in the memory hierarchy.
The idea that increasing the size of a cache always leads to a proportional improvement in performance.
A technique employed by compilers to ensure all frequently used variables are allocated in registers.

questions.question: In the context of cache memory organization, what does 'cache associativity' refer to?
options: The number of cache lines that a particular memory block can be mapped to within a cache set.
The total number of cache blocks available in the entire cache memory.
The speed at which data can be transferred between the cache and main memory.
The time it takes for the CPU to access data stored in the cache.
The policy used to decide which cache line to replace when a cache miss occurs.
